Name: extracellular region
The space external to the outermost structure of a cell. For cells without external protective or external encapsulating structures this refers to space outside of the plasma membrane. This term covers the host cell environment outside an intracellular parasite.
Name: angiotensin II Synonyms: 1-8-angiotensin I, ang II
Name: Ile<small><sup>5</small></sup>-angiotensin II (1-7) Synonyms: 8-Des-phe-angiotensin II, Angiotensin (1-7), Angiotensin I (1-7), Angiotensin II (1-7), Angiotensin II (1-7) heptapeptide

Name: neuroinflammatory response
The immediate defensive reaction by neural vertebrate tissue to infection or injury caused by chemical or physical agents.

Name: astrocyte activation
A change in morphology and behavior of an astrocyte resulting from exposure to a cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or soluble factor.
Name: calcium(2+) Synonyms: CALCIUM ION, Ca2+, Ca<small><sup>2+</small></sup>, calcium, doubly charged positive ion
Name: calcium(2+) Synonyms: CALCIUM ION, Ca2+, Ca<small><sup>2+</small></sup>, calcium, doubly charged positive ion

Name: maintenance of blood-brain barrier Charge: 0
Maintaining the structure and function of the blood-brain barrier, thus ensuring specific regulated transport of substances (e.g. macromolecules, small molecules, ions) into the brain, and out of the brain into the blood circulation.

Name: glial cell apoptotic process
Any apoptotic process in a glial cell, a non-neuronal cell of the nervous system.

Name: neuron apoptotic process
Any apoptotic process in a neuron, the basic cellular unit of nervous tissue. Each neuron consists of a body, an axon, and dendrites. Their purpose is to receive, conduct, and transmit impulses in the nervous system.

Name: regulation of synaptic plasticity
A process that modulates synaptic plasticity, the ability of synapses to change as circumstances require. They may alter function, such as increasing or decreasing their sensitivity, or they may increase or decrease in actual numbers.

Name: syncytium formation by cell-cell fusion
The formation of a syncytium, a mass of cytoplasm containing several nuclei enclosed within a single plasma membrane, by the fusion of the plasma membranes of two or more individual cells.

Name: endothelial cell apoptotic process
Any apoptotic process in an endothelial cell. An endothelial cell comprises the outermost layer or lining of anatomical structures and can be squamous or cuboidal.
